approach.method_basis: The Parent builds molecules by differentiating through a soft version of their structure. It represents each scored molecule as a graph of whole rings and individual atoms, preserves the interior, and makes the identities and presence of selected terminal units and expansion sites adjustable probabilities. A graph encoder learned from unlabeled molecules stays frozen, while a ridge readout is refitted on the current objective's accepted scores. Starting molecules are sampled with a preference for high score rank. The Parent takes bounded gradient steps that increase this readout's predicted value, retains the best relaxed state, then samples structural decisions and compatible attachments to assemble valid, distinct molecules. Accepted products enter the archive and can become later starting structures. The observed limitation is that increasing this point prediction often fails to produce a better assembled molecule.
approach.novelty: The added mechanism is ascent of a lower confidence bound on structural gain. A Gaussian posterior over the existing ridge coefficients estimates how uncertain a proposed change in the frozen graph features is. Structural ascent subtracts one posterior standard deviation of that gain, so a promising but poorly supported direction receives a smaller gradient contribution. The fitted mean remains the Parent's ridge prediction, and the resulting probabilities still drive its existing sampling and assembly process. This lineage contains only its root so far; no sibling has tested coefficient uncertainty inside structural ascent. The experiment asks whether that uncertainty changes the structural updates before sampling, and whether the resulting proposals transfer more reliably to actual improvements.

hypothesis: Replace point-estimate structural ascent with ascent of a numerically smoothed lower confidence bound on relaxed structural gain, subtracting one standard deviation computed from the full Gaussian coefficient posterior associated with the Parent's accepted-only ridge readout and differentiating that uncertainty through the frozen graph encoder.

finding_summary.headline: Uncertainty changed every relaxation, but the mean score fell from 0.3619 to 0.3079
finding_summary.insights:
This experiment establishes that coefficient uncertainty can change structural search before sampling and survive every downstream assembly step. It also shows that correcting this particular source of uncertainty is insufficient to remove prediction optimism or preserve the best final score. The strongest illustration is DRD2: 188 of 290 proposals beat their source, yet the search settled around a much lower score. The molecular assessment describes increasingly crowded polyacetals with late scores near 0.028858, while the Parent's stronger products belonged to a different biaryl/amine series. Repeated small improvements inside a weak chemical family can therefore make source-beating rates look favorable while valuable regions remain unreached.

The evidence leaves open whether the uncertainty penalty restricted productive exploration, whether early stochastic differences redirected the search, or whether structural information missing from the frozen features dominated the remaining errors. The posterior covers coefficient uncertainty conditional on an empirical noise estimate; it does not cover attachment choices, stereochemistry or the gap between a relaxed state and its assembled molecule. The generated structures still exhibit the reactive attachments and unspecified configurations identified by the molecular assessment. Preserving access to alternative core families and representing attachment environments remain worth testing. One paired seed cannot establish the repeatability of the four gains or the DRD2 loss.
finding_summary.results:
The intended mechanism ran throughout this screening replica. All 150 accepted-score posterior fits were valid, all 145 feedback updates changed the full coefficient covariance, and all 152 structural optimizations changed their retained categorical distributions relative to the same starting state's mean-only ascent. Every one of the 1,450 emitted proposals used those changed distributions. All eligible nonzero uncertainty corrections reduced the raw gradient's uncertainty directional derivative, and every optimization retained a positive confidence gain; none needed a fallback.

On the single supplied seed, macro Top-1 fell from 0.361872 to 0.307903, a loss of 0.053969. Four objectives improved: zaleplon_mpo from 0.380139 to 0.394051, deco_hop from 0.589062 to 0.602445, median_2 from 0.180051 to 0.183284, and sitagliptin_mpo from 0.234090 to 0.330875. The loss came from drd2_docking, which fell from 0.426020 to 0.028858. Both runs completed all five 300-evaluation tasks with valid, distinct batches.

Local improvement became more frequent: 447 of 1,450 proposals beat their generating molecule, compared with 380 for the Parent. Predicted improvements were realized 41.1% of the time, up from 32.4%. Their average actual score change nevertheless worsened from -0.025853 to -0.031192, and average overstatement of assembled source-relative gains rose from 0.023479 to 0.034251. Better local hit rates did not produce a better overall search result.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich scaffold series with reactive attachments; the largest products are crowded polyacetals with undefined stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: For n-b3517f183781, the supplied seed-0 trajectories each contain 300 distinct recorded molecules, including 290 optimizer proposals. Every proposal set has ring_closure_rate 1.0 and branch_rate 1.0. The main products are dihydropyrazole-thioureas, extended heteroaryl-substituted indoles, quinoline ethers linked to substituted piperidines, silylmethyl-substituted indole carboxamides, and heavily elaborated polyacetals. Rings, heteroatoms, aromatic groups and saturated amine rings are readily represented. Aromatic-atom presence rates are 1.0 for zaleplon_mpo, deco_hop and median_2, 0.9828 for sitagliptin_mpo, and 0.3379 for the predominantly saturated drd2_docking series. These are presence readings from SMILES text, not aromatic atom fractions or perceived ring counts. The output has many distinct decorations but narrow core families within each trajectory. Ordinary medicinal scaffolds coexist with O-F and N-F bonds, peroxides, chloromethyl ethers, sulfenyl chlorides, primary hydrosilanes and, in a late polyacetal, an explicit carbanion. The most congested polyacetals are difficult to regard as routine synthetic targets. All proposal sets have stereocentre_rate 0.0: configurations are unspecified even where the connectivity implies stereogenic carbons. This does not mean the molecules are achiral. The qualitative quality labels describe the recorded structures; no synthesis, conformer, docking-pose or new property calculation was performed. All supplied objectives are covered. The score readings below are associations in these trajectories and the Parent comparison, not proof of individual substituent effects or a missing target-specific pharmacophore.

method_name: DST: gradient-guided construction through relaxed scaffolding trees
method_thesis: Anchor the method in Differentiable Scaffolding Tree: relax molecular substructure identity and existence into continuous variables, ascend a structural surrogate, and sample discrete structures from the optimized variables. [Fu et al., Sections 3.1-3.3](https://wenhao-gao.github.io/assets/publications/2021_DST_ICLR/paper.pdf) describe this proposal mechanism. For our adaptation, derive an atom/ring token alphabet and train a compact graph encoder by masked-substructure reconstruction solely on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Freeze that encoder and fit a regularized linear scalar readout using only the current objective's accepted observations, updating the readout after feedback. Select scored molecules as local starting structures; hold their internal scaffold context fixed while optimizing relaxed leaf replacement, deletion and expansion variables through the surrogate. Keep surrogate parameters fixed during each structural optimization. Sample edited trees and compatible attachment choices stochastically, assemble new molecules, and repeat generation until the announced batch contains distinct valid structures. The token alphabet supports construction; complete corpus molecules are never retrieved or ranked, and attachment combinations are sampled rather than exhaustively enumerated. Accepted feedback updates both the scored archive and the readout. The hypothesis is that useful structural gradients concentrate new proposals toward real improvements quickly enough to increase the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. Reliable gradients from scarce labels and faithful transfer from relaxed to assembled structures are unproven prerequisites.

activation_observables.measurement: For each ordinary fit, reconstruct the existing ridge mean and the new s2 and full covariance from logged accepted canonical identities and scores, the frozen encoder, fixed normalization, centering and posterior factor. Verify chronological same-objective membership, finite positive posterior variances on nonzero feature differences, and unchanged mean-prediction arithmetic for identical data. Save nonzero feature-difference probes from actual relaxations; evaluate their variance with the old posterior and again immediately after accepted feedback without changing probe identity. Report covariance and probe-variance changes on every nondegenerate update, allowing variance to rise when the fitted noise scale rises. Separate terminal feedback with no later relaxation, zero-difference probes, genuinely degenerate data, and numerical fallbacks. The Parent has no coefficient posterior or such feedback-conditioned uncertainty; its lack of posterior diagnostics is not evidence of zero predictive uncertainty. Freeze checks must include the posterior identity within every structural optimization.
activation_observables.name: accepted_only_gaussian_coefficient_posterior_updates

activation_observables.measurement: At each actual structural state, retain enough data to reconstruct d, the encoder Jacobian pullback, Sigma, smoothed standard deviation and separate gradients g_mean = grad(m) and g_unc = grad(sqrt(d^T Sigma d + epsilon^2)). Verify that the production maximization gradient is g_used = g_mean - g_unc. For states with nonzero g_unc, measure the change in the directional derivative of uncertainty under the raw gradient: g_unc dot g_used minus g_unc dot g_mean must equal -||g_unc||^2 and be strictly negative within numerical tolerance. Report counts, distributions, norms and this arithmetic residual by task and eligible identity/existence family. This diagnostic describes the raw gradient, not a guaranteed reduction in uncertainty after an Adam step. Independently replay the actual Adam step and clipping, and compare its resulting logits with the diagnostic mean-only update from the identical pre-step optimizer state; report nonzero update differences and clipped or degenerate exceptions. The Parent uses g_mean alone and has no uncertainty subtraction. The zero-difference initial state has zero uncertainty gradient by construction and must not be treated as a failed opportunity.
activation_observables.name: posterior_gain_uncertainty_gradient_attenuation

activation_observables.measurement: For every optimization, reconstruct U for the initial state and all visited states under one fixed mean/posterior/encoder identity, verify selection of the highest-U state, and report retained U minus initial U separately from posterior-mean gain and gain standard deviation. Count optimizations with uncertainty-induced step changes and changed retained probabilities relative to a deterministic offline replay of the Parent's mean-only ascent from exactly the same source, sites, initial logits, accepted-data mean and Adam initialization; this replay generates no molecules and uses no oracle. Report cases that retain the initial state, identical optima and clamp saturation separately. Join every emitted molecule to its retained probabilities, sampled structural decisions and compatible attachment choices, and count emitted proposals from relaxations with changed retained distributions. Preserve and audit fixed context, frozen representation, accepted-only means, canonical uniqueness and announced batch sizes. Continue reporting chronological prediction error, assembled predicted-minus-actual source gain and source-beating rates as transfer diagnostics; their improvement is an empirical efficacy question rather than an execution prerequisite.

The Gaussian covariance is conditional on an empirical noise estimate and a linear readout over the existing features. It quantifies uncertainty of those coefficients; it is not a calibrated confidence guarantee for biological activity, representation error, stochastic attachment choices or assembled oracle scores.

The confidence objective compares a relaxed state with that optimization's initial relaxation. It does not establish confidence in a gain relative to the hard source molecule, and favorable relaxed confidence may still fail during discrete sampling or assembly.

A graph encoder learned from unlabeled molecules stays frozen, while a ridge readout is refitted on the current objective's accepted scores. Starting molecules are sampled with a preference for high score rank. The Parent takes bounded gradient steps that increase this readout's predicted value, retains the best relaxed state, then samples structural decisions and compatible attachments to assemble valid, distinct molecules. Accepted products enter the archive and can become later starting structures. The observed limitation is that increasing this point prediction often fails to produce a better assembled molecule.
approach.novelty: The added mechanism is ascent of a lower confidence bound on structural gain. A Gaussian posterior over the existing ridge coefficients estimates how uncertain a proposed change in the frozen graph features is. Structural ascent subtracts one posterior standard deviation of that gain, so a promising but poorly supported direction receives a smaller gradient contribution. The fitted mean remains the Parent's ridge prediction, and the resulting probabilities still drive its existing sampling and assembly process. This lineage contains only its root so far; no sibling has tested coefficient uncertainty inside structural ascent. The experiment asks whether that uncertainty changes the structural updates before sampling, and whether the resulting proposals transfer more reliably to actual improvements.

research_intent.falsifier: The registered mechanism is refuted if full traces show that the covariance is not the specified accepted-only Gaussian ridge covariance, it remains unrelated to nondegenerate accepted feedback, or eligible nonzero gain directions with a nonzero covariance pullback receive no uncertainty gradient correction. Using a diagonal substitute, detaching uncertainty from the structural logits, backpropagating the mean alone, retaining by the mean instead of U, or changing posterior state during an optimization refutes the intended procedure. Complete traces showing no changed structural updates or retained distributions relative to the specified identical-state and identical-start mean-only references, despite nonzero uncertainty corrections and unclipped opportunities, refute the claimed behavioral intervention. Changed retained distributions that are bypassed during actual sampling likewise refute propagation to proposals. Altering the inherited mean fit, frozen representation, structural support or assembly process would confound this one-mechanism experiment. Numerical fallback alone cannot confirm activation; missing trace coverage or an entirely degenerate panel makes the affected claim inconclusive. A zero uncertainty gradient at the initial reference, legitimate retention of that initial state, or a later shared optimum is not individually a falsifier. Correct posterior conditioning and uncertainty-guided structural updates followed by continued prediction optimism or worse final Top-1 constitute negative transfer or score evidence, not a claim that the posterior gradient failed to run.

The Gaussian covariance is conditional on the plug-in empirical noise variance and the linear coefficient model. Its positive values and feedback response are not evidence of calibrated uncertainty for biological activity, representation error, attachment selection or assembled oracle scores.

The smoothed confidence objective is relative to the optimization's initial relaxed state. Initial zero uncertainty gradients and rising uncertainty after a mean/uncertainty tradeoff step are legitimate; conservative initial retention is allowed but was not observed here.

finding_summary.headline: Uncertainty changed every relaxation, but the mean score fell from 0.3619 to 0.3079
finding_summary.insights:
This experiment establishes that coefficient uncertainty can change structural search before sampling and survive every downstream assembly step. It also shows that correcting this particular source of uncertainty is insufficient to remove prediction optimism or preserve the best final score. The strongest illustration is DRD2: 188 of 290 proposals beat their source, yet the search settled around a much lower score. The molecular assessment describes increasingly crowded polyacetals with late scores near 0.028858, while the Parent's stronger products belonged to a different biaryl/amine series. Repeated small improvements inside a weak chemical family can therefore make source-beating rates look favorable while valuable regions remain unreached.

The evidence leaves open whether the uncertainty penalty restricted productive exploration, whether early stochastic differences redirected the search, or whether structural information missing from the frozen features dominated the remaining errors. The posterior covers coefficient uncertainty conditional on an empirical noise estimate; it does not cover attachment choices, stereochemistry or the gap between a relaxed state and its assembled molecule. The generated structures still exhibit the reactive attachments and unspecified configurations identified by the molecular assessment. Preserving access to alternative core families and representing attachment environments remain worth testing. One paired seed cannot establish the repeatability of the four gains or the DRD2 loss.
finding_summary.results:
The intended mechanism ran throughout this screening replica. All 150 accepted-score posterior fits were valid, all 145 feedback updates changed the full coefficient covariance, and all 152 structural optimizations changed their retained categorical distributions relative to the same starting state's mean-only ascent. Every one of the 1,450 emitted proposals used those changed distributions. All eligible nonzero uncertainty corrections reduced the raw gradient's uncertainty directional derivative, and every optimization retained a positive confidence gain; none needed a fallback.

On the single supplied seed, macro Top-1 fell from 0.361872 to 0.307903, a loss of 0.053969. Four objectives improved: zaleplon_mpo from 0.380139 to 0.394051, deco_hop from 0.589062 to 0.602445, median_2 from 0.180051 to 0.183284, and sitagliptin_mpo from 0.234090 to 0.330875. The loss came from drd2_docking, which fell from 0.426020 to 0.028858. Both runs completed all five 300-evaluation tasks with valid, distinct batches.

Local improvement became more frequent: 447 of 1,450 proposals beat their generating molecule, compared with 380 for the Parent. Predicted improvements were realized 41.1% of the time, up from 32.4%. Their average actual score change nevertheless worsened from -0.025853 to -0.031192, and average overstatement of assembled source-relative gains rose from 0.023479 to 0.034251. Better local hit rates did not produce a better overall search result.

finding_summary.headline: Uncertainty changed every relaxation, but the mean score fell from 0.3619 to 0.3079
finding_summary.insights:
This experiment establishes that coefficient uncertainty can change structural search before sampling and survive every downstream assembly step. It also shows that correcting this particular source of uncertainty is insufficient to remove prediction optimism or preserve the best final score. The strongest illustration is DRD2: 188 of 290 proposals beat their source, yet the search settled around a much lower score. The molecular assessment describes increasingly crowded polyacetals with late scores near 0.028858, while the Parent's stronger products belonged to a different biaryl/amine series. Repeated small improvements inside a weak chemical family can therefore make source-beating rates look favorable while valuable regions remain unreached.

The evidence leaves open whether the uncertainty penalty restricted productive exploration, whether early stochastic differences redirected the search, or whether structural information missing from the frozen features dominated the remaining errors. The posterior covers coefficient uncertainty conditional on an empirical noise estimate; it does not cover attachment choices, stereochemistry or the gap between a relaxed state and its assembled molecule. The generated structures still exhibit the reactive attachments and unspecified configurations identified by the molecular assessment. Preserving access to alternative core families and representing attachment environments remain worth testing. One paired seed cannot establish the repeatability of the four gains or the DRD2 loss.

Their average actual score change nevertheless worsened from -0.025853 to -0.031192, and average overstatement of assembled source-relative gains rose from 0.023479 to 0.034251. finding_summary.headline: Uncertainty changed every relaxation, but the mean score fell from 0.3619 to 0.3079
finding_summary.insights:
This experiment establishes that coefficient uncertainty can change structural search before sampling and survive every downstream assembly step. It also shows that correcting this particular source of uncertainty is insufficient to remove prediction optimism or preserve the best final score. The strongest illustration is DRD2: 188 of 290 proposals beat their source, yet the search settled around a much lower score. The molecular assessment describes increasingly crowded polyacetals with late scores near 0.028858, while the Parent's stronger products belonged to a different biaryl/amine series. Repeated small improvements inside a weak chemical family can therefore make source-beating rates look favorable while valuable regions remain unreached.

The evidence leaves open whether the uncertainty penalty restricted productive exploration, whether early stochastic differences redirected the search, or whether structural information missing from the frozen features dominated the remaining errors. The posterior covers coefficient uncertainty conditional on an empirical noise estimate; it does not cover attachment choices, stereochemistry or the gap between a relaxed state and its assembled molecule. The generated structures still exhibit the reactive attachments and unspecified configurations identified by the molecular assessment. Preserving access to alternative core families and representing attachment environments remain worth testing. One paired seed cannot establish the repeatability of the four gains or the DRD2 loss.

All eligible nonzero uncertainty corrections reduced the raw gradient's uncertainty directional derivative, and every optimization retained a positive confidence gain; none needed a fallback.

Local improvement became more frequent: 447 of 1,450 proposals beat their generating molecule, compared with 380 for the Parent. Predicted improvements were realized 41.1% of the time, up from 32.4%. Their average actual score change nevertheless worsened from -0.025853 to -0.031192, and average overstatement of assembled source-relative gains rose from 0.023479 to 0.034251. Better local hit rates did not produce a better overall search result.

applicability_conditions: The evidence motivating this Child is specific to the Parent's one supplied screening replica. The protocol must establish any score effect and reliability using its assigned evaluations.

The Parent must supply eligible structural variables, a frozen differentiable graph representation, and nondegenerate accepted feature/score data. All posterior fitting remains local to the current objective.

The Gaussian covariance is conditional on an empirical noise estimate and a linear readout over the existing features. It quantifies uncertainty of those coefficients; it is not a calibrated confidence guarantee for biological activity, representation error, stochastic attachment choices or assembled oracle scores.

The confidence objective compares a relaxed state with that optimization's initial relaxation. It does not establish confidence in a gain relative to the hard source molecule, and favorable relaxed confidence may still fail during discrete sampling or assembly.

The proposed benefit requires unsupported feature directions to contribute to the Parent's optimism. If missing structural information or attachment ambiguity dominates, uncertainty in the existing coefficients may leave that optimism intact.

Subtracting uncertainty can suppress useful exploration or retain an initial relaxed distribution. The existing stochastic generator must still produce complete valid distinct batches, and reduced exploration may lower final Top-1 even when every registered intermediate calculation is correct.

There is no active Development Layer or previous Child in this lineage and the supplied cluster history is empty. This is a new test of posterior uncertainty inside structural ascent, with the inherited method stack preserved.

approach.method_basis: The Parent builds molecules by differentiating through a soft version of their structure. It represents each scored molecule as a graph of whole rings and individual atoms, preserves the interior, and makes the identities and presence of selected terminal units and expansion sites adjustable probabilities. A graph encoder learned from unlabeled molecules stays frozen, while a ridge readout is refitted on the current objective's accepted scores. Starting molecules are sampled with a preference for high score rank. The Parent takes bounded gradient steps that increase this readout's predicted value, retains the best relaxed state, then samples structural decisions and compatible attachments to assemble valid, distinct molecules. Accepted products enter the archive and can become later starting structures. The observed limitation is that increasing this point prediction often fails to produce a better assembled molecule.
approach.novelty: The added mechanism is ascent of a lower confidence bound on structural gain. A Gaussian posterior over the existing ridge coefficients estimates how uncertain a proposed change in the frozen graph features is. Structural ascent subtracts one posterior standard deviation of that gain, so a promising but poorly supported direction receives a smaller gradient contribution. The fitted mean remains the Parent's ridge prediction, and the resulting probabilities still drive its existing sampling and assembly process. This lineage contains only its root so far; no sibling has tested coefficient uncertainty inside structural ascent. The experiment asks whether that uncertainty changes the structural updates before sampling, and whether the resulting proposals transfer more reliably to actual improvements.

research_intent.falsifier: The registered mechanism is refuted if full traces show that the covariance is not the specified accepted-only Gaussian ridge covariance, it remains unrelated to nondegenerate accepted feedback, or eligible nonzero gain directions with a nonzero covariance pullback receive no uncertainty gradient correction. Using a diagonal substitute, detaching uncertainty from the structural logits, backpropagating the mean alone, retaining by the mean instead of U, or changing posterior state during an optimization refutes the intended procedure. Complete traces showing no changed structural updates or retained distributions relative to the specified identical-state and identical-start mean-only references, despite nonzero uncertainty corrections and unclipped opportunities, refute the claimed behavioral intervention. Changed retained distributions that are bypassed during actual sampling likewise refute propagation to proposals. Altering the inherited mean fit, frozen representation, structural support or assembly process would confound this one-mechanism experiment. Numerical fallback alone cannot confirm activation; missing trace coverage or an entirely degenerate panel makes the affected claim inconclusive. A zero uncertainty gradient at the initial reference, legitimate retention of that initial state, or a later shared optimum is not individually a falsifier. Correct posterior conditioning and uncertainty-guided structural updates followed by continued prediction optimism or worse final Top-1 constitute negative transfer or score evidence, not a claim that the posterior gradient failed to run.
